finalists.why: It has the most specific and decisive findings, including a positive nasopharyngeal swab and anosmia.

finalists.label: Sepsis
finalists.why: It is supported by fever, low oxygen saturation, and a positive nasopharyngeal swab, which are all indicative of a severe infection.

finalists.label: Pneumonia
finalists.why: Although not directly listed in this group, Pneumonia is a strong candidate due to the chest radiography and clinical presentation, but it is already well-represented in the commit group.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a positive nasopharyngeal swab by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction and specific symptoms like anosmia make COVID-19 the most likely diagnosis.
